conflicts.description: Ring Seven demands recognition and fair terms while the Concord demands the elevators reopened and the harvest shared, with the water valves as leverage.
conflicts.name: Bread and Independence

conflicts.description: The Shaft Climbers are courted by both sides and may decide the outcome by choosing whom to carry or betray.
conflicts.name: The Climbers' Price

description: The generation ship Halcyon Meridian has sailed for two centuries as a vertical stack of nine rotating habitat tiers, each one a ring joined to the others by a spine of elevators. The seventh ring, the agricultural and water-reclamation heart of the vessel, has just declared independence and severed the elevators that connect the habitable tiers. Ring Seven now controls the water and grain that every other ring depends on. This is a tense science fiction story about scarcity, rotation physics, and the question of who owns a closed world. Every decision is made under the pressure of failing margins. Control of the elevators means control of food, air pressure balance, and the ship's ability to correct its course. The ring that feeds the ship wants a voice. The rings above and below it want their bread back. Nobody can leave, and nobody can afford a war that breaches a hull.

factions.description: The elected council of Ring Seven farmers and reclamation engineers who voted to secede and sever the elevators.
factions.name: Seventh Assembly

factions.description: The traditional ship government that insists the ring is a mutiny and wants unified control restored.
factions.name: Concord of Helm

factions.description: A guild of maintenance workers who know the elevator shafts better than anyone and sell passage to both sides.
factions.name: Shaft Climbers

history.description: The Halcyon Meridian leaves its home system with all nine rings joined by the elevator spine.
history.name: The Departure

history.description: A grain blight cuts rations across the ship and leaves Ring Seven feeling blamed and unrewarded for its labor.
history.name: The Blight Year

history.description: The Concord imposes a larger share of Ring Seven's harvest as tithe, sparking organized protest.
history.name: The Ration Tithe

history.description: Seventh Assembly crews lock and sever the elevator couplings, stranding cabins in the shafts.
history.name: The Severance

locations.description: The curved agricultural ring where tiered paddies and hydroponic galleries wrap overhead in the spin gravity. It is the seat of the independence movement and the ship's main food source.
locations.name: Ring Seven Terraces

locations.description: The central elevator columns linking every ring. Their severed cabins hang frozen between tiers, and the shafts are now a dangerous no-man's land of climbing crews and sabotage.
locations.name: Spine Elevator Shafts

locations.description: The forward-most ring housing navigation, command, and the ship's governing Concord. It is isolated from fresh produce and increasingly desperate to restore the link.
locations.name: Helm Ring One

locations.description: A flooded reclamation vault beneath Ring Seven where the ship's water is purified. Whoever holds its valves can starve the other rings of drinking water.
locations.name: Cistern Undercroft

name: The Tessellate Ring Stack

rules.statement: Gravity exists only through ring rotation, and any large asymmetric change in mass or a stalled ring threatens the balance of the whole stack.
The atmosphere is a closed loop; a hull breach in any ring causes rapid pressure loss that cannot be replaced from outside.
Only the spine elevators move people and cargo between rings; there is no alternate transport that can carry bulk goods.
Chemical explosives are banned across the vessel because any blast risks a fatal breach, so conflict relies on tools, sabotage, and control of resources.
All water is tracked in a shared ledger, and the ring that controls reclamation is treated as holding a public trust.
